pr_title: Add map update tracking to MapCache
pr_body:
fixes #20012

I also update LobbyLogic to use this new logic, it reduces maintenance overhead
pr_comments: Are we able to use this to fix #19988 too?

> Are we able to use this to fix #19988 too?

I will just update #19990 to depend on this pr. Really it is already ready to merge, all I can do is just add smart updating to it (which just became very easy with this pr)
I meant that applying the approach from `RestartGame` to `ServerCreationLogic.CreateAndJoin` should fix https://github.com/OpenRA/OpenRA/pull/19990/files#r858018992 and make that PR unnecessary(?)

> I meant that applying the approach from `RestartGame` to `ServerCreationLogic.CreateAndJoin` should fix https://github.com/OpenRA/OpenRA/pull/19990/files#r858018992 and make that PR unnecessary(?)

I disagree on such an approach. As I mentioned in that PR I find my approach more intuitive and user friendly, it mimics the behaviour of `LobbyLogic`, and to some extent, `MissionBrowser`

I notice that the map tracker maintains a `FileSystemWatcher` for each map directory and all files in it. That is usefull during map editing. But is it needed in game? Wouldn't it be better to only enable this functionality with a start up flag or setting checkbox?

How many maps does a player have in the map directory? File watching can be slow on slow old systems with many files to watch. (Can you even watch for filename changes/moves on Linux?)

`LastUpdatedMap` how about `LastExternallyModifiedMap`. As i read the code, when you restart a game it will reload any other map that was last modified on disk? So this could also be a different map? I guess this is what you want as editor.

Map cache code flow is somewhat difficult to read. The directory trackers call `LoadMap` as well as `MapCache.LoadMap` does. Seems cleaner if `MapCache` would receive events from the trackers and reload maps by itself based on the event? Both classes/object call eachother in each direction.

With now `mapUpdates` it seems updates are coming from multiple sides? I.e. you add an additional layer to track the same changes?

Seems incorrect that `mapUpdates` is only added to never removed?

Entries for old maps/hashes remain in the cache? This might be ok - assuming there won't be many updates over time.

> I notice that the map tracker maintains a `FileSystemWatcher` for each map directory and all files in it. That is usefull during map editing. But is it needed in game? Wouldn't it be better to only enable this functionality with a start up flag or setting checkbox?
>
> How many maps does a player have in the map directory? File watching can be slow on slow old systems with many files to watch. (Can you even watch for filename changes/moves on Linux?

Afaik it works on linux, pretty sure someone had tested that. About performance I dunno, my code shouldn't have any impact, but I have no idea about `FileSystemWatcher`. Tbh I never even considered it, just followed pchotes suggestion to use it

> Seems incorrect that `mapUpdates` is only added to never removed?
> 
> Entries for old maps/hashes remain in the cache? This might be ok - assuming there won't be many updates over time.

That's how the system worked before I implemented updates. Outdated maps get disabled, but not deleted from memory. Because of that I implemented a system that only adds a new map when necessary, as I don't want to clog up memory.

I'll take a deeper look into your other suggestions later, when I get back home tomorrow.

> `LastUpdatedMap` how about `LastExternallyModifiedMap`. As i read the code, when you restart a game it will reload any other map that was last modified on disk? So this could also be a different map? I guess this is what you want as editor.

I'm renaming to `LastModifiedMap`. I cannot name it external as map editor is also tracked. 
This does not track anything on game restart as the game doesn't keep track of files without being turned on. Rather files are tracked during runtime and MapCache is updated whenever a map is requested by any part of the code, during runtime

> Map cache code flow is somewhat difficult to read. The directory trackers call `LoadMap` as well as `MapCache.LoadMap` does. Seems cleaner if `MapCache` would receive events from the trackers and reload maps by itself based on the event? Both classes/object call eachother in each direction.

What you are basically suggesting is moving `MapDirectoryTracker` class into `MapCache`. We can't use events without moving basically all tracking logic to `MapCache`. We could of course do that and stack `MapCache` even harder. I wouldn't oppose it but I don't really see point so it won't be me doing the refactoring.

> With now `mapUpdates` it seems updates are coming from multiple sides? I.e. you add an additional layer to track the same changes?

I'm not really sure what you mean. Values get added to it only from `LoadMap` method

issue_context.title: Restarting a map after changing the Lua script crashes with a map not found exception
issue_context.body:
```
Exception of type `System.InvalidOperationException`: Map 016ee2032e81e5d7bbda6d1ea0bbb0509b1bfab7 not found
   at OpenRA.Mods.Common.Server.LobbyCommands.ServerStarted(Server server) in \OpenRA\OpenRA.Mods.Common\ServerTraits\LobbyCommands.cs:line 1134
   at OpenRA.Server.Server.<>c__DisplayClass52_0.<.ctor>b__2(Object _) in \OpenRA\OpenRA.Game\Server\Server.cs:line 346
   at System.Threading.Thread.StartCallback()
```
Easiest testcase is starting a mission, editing the Lua script and then restarting. Might also crash when yaml changes are applied.
comments: IMO this is a major use case for the map reindexing feature, so the map cache really should be able to remap from the old UID to the new one so the restart feature can behave as you'd expect.

review_comments: I'm not really sure what name to use here
